raw: {"analysis": "Both responses provide comprehensive delivery plans addressing the webhook migration, buffering, approvals, and rollback. ZLZ stands out by explicitly including a simulation tool (Lane D) to generate out-of-sequence, delayed, and duplicate events, directly targeting the core tricky part of the request. It also gives a more concrete rollback action for the buffer (discard contents) and proactively isolates the flaky test. ZLQ offers a canary deployment and a data integrity audit, but lacks a dedicated simulation harness for out-of-order scenarios and is slightly less specific on buffer rollback. Both correctly handle irreversible schema and approval gates, but ZLZ's focus on testing the exact failure mode makes it more helpful for the requester.", "verdict": "ZLZ"}
